title: Geography-led pricing & contract experiment: EU/UK residency, SCCs, subprocessors, and retention
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Run a two-phased experiment to validate a geography-tiered pricing and contract playbook for enterprise customers that need EU/UK data residency, explicit SCCs, limited subprocessors, and configurable retention. Goal: find viable price delta and standardized contract language that reduces sales cycle time while keeping legal and infra risk acceptable.
background: We frequently field enterprise RFPs asking for EU/UK residency, SCCs + EU data processing addenda, strict retention windows, and tight subprocessors lists. Sales currently escalates to Legal with ad-hoc pricing. This causes long cycles and inconsistent offers. We need a repeatable playbook pairing pricing tiers with a clear set of contract commitments and a minimal engineering implementation scope for Private/Dedicated options.
objectives: Quantify customer willingness-to-pay for 'EU-only residency + SCCs' vs 'global with contractual controls'
Produce a canonical contract appendix (SLA/retention/subprocessors/SCCs) that Legal can accept for initial offers
Define infra scoping (Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted with egress controls) and estimate one-time engineering lift
Measure sales cycle time reduction and acceptance rate across pilot accounts
success_metrics: Acceptance rate >= 40% for pilot offers within target segments (Fintech, HealthTech, Gov)
Median sales cycle reduction from 72 days to <= 40 days for offers using the playbook
Clear price delta bandwidth identified: low/medium/high residency tiers with target ASP uplift percentages
Engineering implementation plan with <= 6 week critical path for minimally required infra changes
scope_inclusions: Contract appendix text for EU/UK SCCs + DPA clauses (approved by Legal)
Residency product definitions: Hosted-EU (logical + geo routing), Dedicated-EU (reserved capacity in EU cloud regions), Private-VPC (customer-managed networking)
Retention control options: 30/90/365 days, with optional strict delete within 30 days for add-on
Subprocessor commitments: predefined allow-list + process for approval of additional subprocessors
out_of_scope: Custom engineering for on-prem air-gapped deployments (handled via Private channel separately)
Full rework of billing platform — only pricing docs and tooling hooks for quoting included
Major encryption-scheme redesigns (KMS integrations will use existing patterns)
assumptions: Legal will accept a limited set of standard SCCs and a DPA template for pilot customers
Engineering can deliver necessary routing + storage partitioning with low-to-medium effort
Sales will engage 8–12 pilot accounts representative of target segments within 6 weeks
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Legal pushes for bespoke clauses — Mitigation: escalate to Legal leadership with a 'deal corridor' that limits bespoke edits and introduces surcharge for custom terms
Risk: Engineering underestimates storage separation complexity — Mitigation: quick spike (ENG-2489) and allocate buffer in timeline
Risk: Customers expect on-prem full isolation — Mitigation: clearly document Private vs On-prem tradeoffs and route on-prem requests to Solutions Engineering
pricing_hypotheses: H1: 'EU Residency + SCCs' can command a 20–35% ASP uplift over base hosted pricing for high-reg customers
H2: 'Retention-lowered' offers (30-day delete) can be a $X/month add-on with high conversion for regulated verticals
H3: Fixed-term committed Dedicated capacity discounts will be required to make Dedicated-EU economically attractive to mid-market
proposal_summary: Create three canonical offers: (A) Hosted-EU with SCCs and standard DPA (small premium), (B) Dedicated-EU reserved pools with contractual retention controls (mid premium + commit), (C) Private VPC with strict retention and limited subprocessors (enterprise-premium + implementation fee). Publish price bands and create quote templates for sales.
deliverables: Draft contract appendix (DPA + SCCs + subprocessor table)
Pricing bands and quote templates for three offers
Engineering spike report and implementation plan (ENG-2231, ENG-2489)
Pilot launch checklist and 8–12 pilot account list
acceptance_criteria: Legal-signed DPA appendix checked into Confluence and GitHub (link in attachments)
Pricing bands validated by 3 pilot deals or calibrated through negotiated pilots
Engineering plan with milestones and owners and budget estimate approved
Sales materials complete and at least 3 pilot engagements committed
timeline: Week 0-1: Legal DPA draft and pricing hypothesis workshop (completed)
Week 2: Engineering spike and infra scoping (ENG-2231/ENG-2489)
Week 3-4: Sales pilot outreach and initial quotes
Week 5-7: Pilot negotiations, collect conversion data
Week 8: Retrospective and final playbook publication
